policy: Historical event dates only. A scheduled calendar slot is not an anniversary. Retain year-only precision when an exact day has not been established, especially person-focused stories anchored to a work rather than a birthday. Region qualifiers distinguish launches.

overrides.event: First public demonstration

source.title: The First Video Game?
source.supports: The laboratory dates the first public introduction to October 18, 1958, at its visitors day.

overrides.event: Original Game Boy Japanese launch

source.title: Game Boy (DMG-01): original hardware catalogue
source.supports: Original manufacturer page directly states release date 1989-04-21. HTML decoded as CP932/Shift-JIS; the date is text, not inferred from Super Mario Land.

overrides.event: Japanese hardware launch

source.title: PlayStation 2 reaches 50 million units
source.supports: The retrospective press release states Japan March 4, 2000; North America October 26; Europe/PAL November 24.

overrides.note: Date shown is the Japanese launch, not a single worldwide release date.

overrides.event: Original Nintendo 3DS Japanese launch

source.title: Nintendo 3DS: original hardware page
source.supports: Manufacturer page states 2011.2.26 release. Also confirmed by Nintendo June 2, 2011 corporate announcement.

overrides.note: Date refers to the original Japanese hardware launch, not the later Zelda anniversary finish depicted by some models.

overrides.event: Original PC shareware release

source.title: DOOM Turns 22!
source.supports: Publisher anniversary article explicitly dates the original DOOM to December 10, 1993. The article body is English despite its locale path.

overrides.event: General PlayStation Network release

source.title: Journey Takes Its First Steps This March
source.supports: Creative director announces March 13, 2012 general PSN availability.

overrides.note: Date marks the North American general release. PlayStation Plus early access preceded it, and European general release followed on March 14; it is not claimed as the first availability anywhere.

overrides.event: Original desktop release

source.title: Games by Lucas Pope: Papers, Please
source.supports: Developer catalogue places August 8, 2013 below the Papers, Please original release record, separately from the public beta and later games.

overrides.event: Original 2018 release, Xbox One availability verified

source.title: Celeste Is Now Available For Xbox One
source.supports: Platform holder published its now-available launch notice on January 25, 2018; this corroborates the original 2018 release rather than later platform ports.

overrides.event: Original Nintendo Switch launch

source.title: Switch and Play: A More Active Game Life
source.supports: Corporate announcement identifies March 3, 2017 simultaneous launch in Japan, United States, Canada, major European countries, Australia and Hong Kong.

overrides.note: Initial markets launched together; the source says additional countries followed by the end of March, so the date is not labelled universal availability.

overrides.event: Original Nintendo Switch release

source.title: Super Mario Bros. Wonder: Nintendo Switch product record
source.supports: Official original Nintendo Switch product details state 20/10/2023 for both game card and download version. Later Switch 2 edition promotions do not replace that original record.

overrides.event: Nintendo Switch presentation livestream in North American time zones

source.title: Nintendo Switch Presentation 2017 coming January 13th 2017
source.type: Primary: presentation schedule and explicit time-zone conversion
source.supports: Official updated schedule states live from Tokyo on January 13, 2017 at 04:00 UK time. January UK time is GMT; this instant is January 12 at 23:00 EST / 20:00 PST. The North American calendar day is an explicit time-zone conversion, not a guessed launch date.

overrides.note: Presentation occurred January 13 in Tokyo/Europe and January 12 in North America. This stop is separate from the March 3 hardware launch.
